steps: The Vertical Milling Machine mills a keyway into the Shaft Rough Cut, which is a lathed part, using a speed of 1200 rpm, an end mill tool, and a depth of cut of 2 mm for 53 minutes, producing the Shaft with Keyway, a milled part, which is then moved to a mobile robot.

The Precision Keyway Finishing operation is performed using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) for 48 minutes on a Shaft with Keyway, utilizing a brass wire, a cutting speed of 3 mm/min, and an electrical parameter of 220 V, resulting in a Shaft with Precision Keyway.

Using a Horizontal Lathe, the Rough Turning operation transforms a Steel Bar on a ConveyorBelt into a Rough Turned Shaft at a rotation speed of 800 rpm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and with a Carbide Insert tool, taking 17 minutes to complete, with the final product placed on a MobileRobot.

The steel bar is subjected to rough turning for 42 minutes on a vertical lathe at 600 rpm rotation speed, using a carbide insert tool with a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, transforming it into a rough turned shaft, which is then placed on a mobile robot.
Using a Gear Shaper machine, the Gear Shaping operation transforms a Broached Gear Blank into a Shaped Gear with 24 teeth at a shaping speed of 100 strokes/min for 70 minutes.
Using a Bandsaw, a Steel Bar from the ConveyorBelt is cut into a LathedPart (Cut Bar) on a MobileRobot for 99 minutes with a saw speed of 50 m/min, a Bi-metal blade, and a cutting width of 3 mm.

Using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine, the operation involves shearing a Steel Sheet from the ConveyorBelt into a Sheared Sheet, which is then placed on a MobileRobot, with a shear angle of 1.5 degrees, a cutting speed of 10 m/min, and a straight blade, for 23 minutes.
Using a Punch Press, the operation Punching transforms a Steel Sheet into a Punched Sheet by employing a 10 mm punch at a speed of 40 strokes/min with centered die alignment, lasting for 79 minutes.

The Surface Grinding operation is performed on Grinding Machines for 42 minutes, using an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at a speed of 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, to transform a Planed Shaft into a Ground Shaft, both transported by a MobileRobot.

Using Screw Machines, the Threading operation transforms a Turned Shaft into a Shaft with Threads, processing for 88 minutes with parameters including an M12 screw size, Metric thread type, and a production rate of 50 parts/hour.

The Planing operation planes a Milled Shaft for 23 minutes on a Planer, using a planing depth of 0.1 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 m/min, and achieving a surface finish of Ra 1.6, transforming it into a Planed Shaft.
The Hobbing Machine performs Gear Hobbing on a Broached Gear Blank for 77 minutes at a hobbing speed of 80 rpm and a feed rate of 1 mm/rev to produce a Hobbied Gear with an involute profile.

Using a Drill Press, perform a Drilling operation on a Steel Bar from the ConveyorBelt for 59 minutes with an 8 mm drill bit, a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev to produce a Drilled Bar, which is then placed on a MobileRobot.

The Laser Cutting operation uses a Laser Cutter for 45 minutes to transform a Steel Sheet into a Laser Cut Sheet, employing a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 0.8 m/min, and nitrogen as the assist gas.

The Honing Machine performs honing on a Rough Honed Cylinder for 84 minutes using a 220 grit honing tool, a cycle time of 10 minutes, and a bore size of 50 mm, resulting in a Precision Honed Cylinder.

The Broaching Machine performs the Broaching operation on a Steel Bar for 58 minutes using a Push Broach with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/stroke and a depth of cut of 1 mm, transforming it into a Broached Bar placed on a MobileRobot.

The Stewart Platform Mills perform Precision Milling on a Milled Shaft for 47 minutes using a Ball Nose tool with a milling precision of 0.001 mm and active vibration damping, transforming it into a Finished Shaft, which is then placed in a MobileRobot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Finish Milling on a Milled Shaft for 91 minutes at a milling speed of 1000 rpm using a contour tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8, transforming the Milled Shaft into a Finished Shaft, which is then transferred to a MobileRobot.

Using a Shaper machine for 29 minutes, the Shaping operation transforms a Milled Shaft into a Shaped Shaft by employing a Single Point tool with a stroke length of 100 mm and a shaping speed of 50 strokes per minute, with both the input and output components handled by a MobileRobot.

The Finish Turning operation on the CNC Turning Center processes a Turned Shaft into a Finished Shaft using G-code with a spindle speed of 1500 rpm and tool offsets of 0.05 mm, lasting for 48 minutes.
The hobbing operation transforms the input broached gear into an output involute-profile hobbied gear using a hobbing machine at a speed of 200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev for 52 minutes.

The Gear Shaping operation shapes a BroachedComponent Input Gear into a ShapedGear Output Gear using a Gear Shaper machine, processing for 74 minutes at a shaping speed of 150 rpm to create a Spur gear with 20 teeth.

Using a Vertical Lathe, perform Turning on an Input Bar made of MetalBar to produce an Output Part of type LathedPart for 35 minutes, with a rotation speed of 300 rpm, a carbide tool, and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev.

The Precision Milling operation uses a Stewart Platform Mills to transform an Input Part (a MilledPart on a ConveyorBelt) into an Output Part (a GroundPart on a ConveyorBelt) for 3 minutes, with a milling precision of 0.01 mm, a Ball Nose tool configuration, and active vibration damping.

Grinding Machines process the Input Part, a PlanedPart from the ConveyorBelt, into a GroundPart using an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, completing the operation in 45 minutes.

Using a Punch Press, punch the Input Sheet made of SheetMetal into an Output Sheet of CutSheetMetal for 36 minutes, with a punch size of 10 mm, a stroke speed of 50 spm, and a die alignment within a 0.02 mm tolerance, transferring both components on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a Screw Machines, perform a Threading operation on a LathedPart from the ConveyorBelt for 92 minutes with an M10 screw size and Metric thread type at a production rate of 100 units/hour, resulting in a ScrewedComponent placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Planer machine performs a Planing operation on an Input Part (a MilledPart from the ConveyorBelt) for 20 minutes, producing an Output Part (a PlanedPart on the ConveyorBelt) with a Planing depth of 2 mm, a Feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and a Surface finish of 16 microinches.

The input milled part is loaded from the conveyor belt into a Horizontal Milling Machine for a contour milling process at 250 rpm, achieving a surface finish of 32 microinches, and is output as a finished machined component onto the conveyor belt after 58 minutes of operation.

The Shaping operation transforms an Input Part (MilledPart) from the ConveyorBelt into an Output Part (ShapedPart) on the ConveyorBelt using a Shaper machine for 14 minutes, with a stroke length of 200 mm, a shaping speed of 30 spm, and an HSS tool type.

The Cutting operation on the Bandsaw processes an Input Bar (MetalBar) from the ConveyorBelt into an Output Part (LathedPart) on the ConveyorBelt for 5 minutes using a Bimetal blade at a saw speed of 50 m/min and a cutting width of 2 mm.

Using a Drill Press for 93 minutes, the operation drills an Input Bar (MetalBar) from the ConveyorBelt into an Output Part (DrilledComponent) on the same ConveyorBelt with a 12 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 600 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning on a lathed input part from the conveyor belt for 46 minutes using a CNC program of G01 X50 Z20, tool offsets of X0.1 Z0.05, and a spindle speed of 800 rpm to produce a finished machined component, which is then placed back onto the conveyor belt.
The Broaching Machine performs broaching for 36 minutes to transform an Input Bar into an Output Part using a Push broach with a feed rate of 0.05 mm/rev and a depth of cut of 1.5 mm.

The Honing Machine performs the honing operation on an Input Cylinder for 94 minutes, using a honing grit size of 400, a cycle time of 5 minutes, and a bore size of 50 mm, transforming it into a Precision finished part placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The Shearing operation cuts an input sheet of sheet metal into a sheared sheet metal output using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 76 minutes, with a shear angle of 2 degrees, a cutting speed of 30 m/min, and a straight blade.

Using a Horizontal Lathe, the operation of Turning transforms an Input Bar (MetalBar) on a ConveyorBelt into an Output Part (LathedPart) on a ConveyorBelt for 63 minutes, with a rotation speed of 350 rpm, a carbide tool, and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev.

The Laser Cutting operation uses a Laser Cutter to cut an Input Sheet of SheetMetal into an Output Sheet of Cut sheet metal for 95 minutes, with a laser power of 2000 W, a cutting speed of 10 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist, with both input and output components handled on a ConveyorBelt.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs milling for 66 minutes at a speed of 300 rpm using an end mill with a 5 mm depth of cut, transforming a LathedPart from the conveyor belt into a MilledPart placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) operation precisely cuts a shaped input part using a brass wire at a cutting speed of 5 mm/min with electrical parameters of 40 V and 10 A, transforming it into a precision finished part over 49 minutes.

The Hydraulic Cylinder Rod, initially in a milled state on the conveyor belt, undergoes a shaping operation on the Shaper machine for 42 minutes using a carbide tool with a stroke length of 500 mm and a shaping speed of 20 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped part placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Shearing operation cuts Sheet Metal into CutSheetMetal using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 62 minutes with a shear angle of 2 degrees, a cutting speed of 10 m/min, and a high-carbon steel blade, transferring the output to the conveyor belt.

The bandsaw performs a cutting operation on a metal bar from the conveyor belt, using a bi-metal blade at a speed of 50 m/min with a cutting width of 10 mm, transforming it into a lathed part on the conveyor belt for 83 minutes.

Using a Grinding Machine for 59 minutes, the Hydraulic Cylinder Rod, initially a PlanedPart on the ConveyorBelt, is ground into a GroundPart with an Aluminum oxide grinding wheel operating at 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/pass, and is placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Horizontal Lathe performs a Turning operation on a Metal Bar for 60 minutes, using a Carbide insert tool with a rotation speed of 1200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, transforming the Metal Bar into a Lathed Part which remains on the Conveyor Belt.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs milling on a Hydraulic Cylinder Rod for 8 minutes, using an end mill at 500 rpm with a depth of cut of 2 mm, transforming it from a lathed part into a milled part, which remains on the conveyor belt.

The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on a broached gear blank for 15 minutes at a hobbing speed of 100 rpm and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev to produce an involute-profile hobbied gear, which is then placed on the conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs Electrical Discharge Machining on a Hydraulic Cylinder Rod, transforming it into a precision finished part, using a brass wire at 220 V and 10 A with a cutting speed of 5 mm/min for 10 minutes.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Finish Milling on a Hydraulic Cylinder Rod for 1 minute at a milling speed of 600 rpm with a contour tool path to achieve a surface finish of 0.8 µm, transforming it into a finished machined component that remains on the conveyor belt.

The Planing operation smooths the Hydraulic Cylinder Rod using a Planer for 78 minutes with a planing depth of 3 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, and a surface finish of 1.6 µm, transforming the MilledPart into a PlanedPart while keeping it on the ConveyorBelt.
The Gear Shaping operation transforms a BroachedComponent Gear Blank into a ShapedGear using a Gear Shaper machine for 27 minutes, shaping a Spur gear with 20 teeth at a speed of 80 rpm.
The Broaching Machine performs keyway broaching on a metal bar, using a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev and a depth of cut of 5 mm, transforming the metal bar into a broached component, for 98 minutes.

The Punch Press performs a punching operation on sheet metal for 35 minutes, using a punch size of 10 mm, a stroke speed of 60 strokes/min, and a die alignment of 0.01 mm, transforming it into a finished sheet metal product.

Using a Vertical Lathe, the Turning operation is performed on a Metal Bar for 22 minutes at a rotation speed of 1500 rpm, a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, and using a CBN insert tool, transforming the Metal Bar into a LathedPart which is then placed on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a Drill Press, the operation drills an 8 mm hole into a Metal Bar placed on the ConveyorBelt at a spindle speed of 1000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev for 80 minutes, transforming it into a DrilledComponent still on the ConveyorBelt.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning on a Hydraulic Cylinder Rod for 77 minutes using the Cylinder Rod program, a 0.5 mm tool offset, and a spindle speed of 800 rpm, transforming the lathed part into a finished machined component, both handled via the conveyor belt.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs Precision Milling on a Hydraulic Cylinder Rod, converting it from a MilledPart to a GroundPart, using a ball nose end mill with a milling precision of 0.01 mm and active vibration damping, for 86 minutes, with the component being processed and output on the ConveyorBelt.

The Honing Machine performs honing on a Hydraulic Cylinder from the ConveyorBelt using a 400 grit honing tool and a 50 mm bore size, with a cycle time of 10 minutes, transforming it into a precision finished part in 63 minutes.
The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on Sheet Metal for 44 minutes using a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 1.5 m/min, and Nitrogen gas assist, transforming it into Cut Sheet Metal.

The Hydraulic Cylinder Rod, initially a lathed part on the conveyor belt, undergoes screw machining on the Screw Machines for 39 minutes, using an M8 screw size with a metric thread type at a production rate of 10 parts per minute, resulting in a screwed component placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Shaper machine performs the Shaping operation on a MilledPart Gear Shaft for 10 minutes, using a Carbide tool with a stroke length of 200 mm and a shaping speed of 50 strokes/min, transforming it into a ShapedPart Gear Shaft on the ConveyorBelt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs Precision Cutting on a Gear Shaft for 6 minutes using a Brass wire, with electrical parameters set to 50V and 10A at a cutting speed of 2 mm/min, transforming the shaped part into a precision finished part.

The Honing Machine performs the Honing operation on a Gear Shaft, transforming it from a HonedCylinder to a Precision finished part, using a honing grit size of 400, a cycle time of 60 seconds, and a bore size of 50 mm, for 62 minutes.

Using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine, the Gear Shaft, initially a SheetMetal component on the ConveyorBelt, is sheared for 67 minutes at a 90-degree shear angle and a cutting speed of 10 m/min with a High-Speed Steel blade, resulting in a ShearedSheetMetal Gear Shaft placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Planer machine performs planing on a Gear Shaft milled part from the conveyor belt for 66 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2 mm, a feed rate of 5 mm/min, and a surface finish of 0.8 Ra, resulting in a planed Gear Shaft placed back on the conveyor belt.

Using a Laser Cutter for 38 minutes, perform Laser Cutting on a SheetMetal Gear Shaft from the ConveyorBelt, with a laser power of 1500 W, a cutting speed of 10 mm/s, and Nitrogen gas assist, to produce a CutSheetMetal Gear Shaft placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The bandsaw performs the sawing operation on a metal bar gear shaft taken from the conveyor belt, using a bimetal blade at a speed of 50 m/min with a cutting width of 5 mm, transforming it into a lathed part placed back on the conveyor belt, for 20 minutes.

The Horizontal Lathe performs turning on a Gear Shaft, converting it from a MetalBar to a LathedPart, using a rotation speed of 1200 rpm, a carbide tool, and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, for 76 minutes.

The Vertical Lathe performs the Turning operation on a Gear Shaft (a MetalBar) for 94 minutes using a High-Speed Steel tool at a rotation speed of 1000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, transforming it into a LathedPart that remains on the ConveyorBelt.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs a precision milling operation on a Gear Shaft, transforming it from a MilledPart to a GroundPart with a precision of 0.01 mm using a 4-flute end mill and active vibration damping, taking 67 minutes to complete.

The Punch Press performs a Punching operation on a Gear Shaft (sheet metal) for 34 minutes, using a 10 mm punch size, a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min, and a die alignment of 0.1 mm, transforming it into a finished sheet metal product, with both input and output components being conveyed on a conveyor belt.

The Drill Press performs the Drilling operation on a metal bar Gear Shaft for 59 minutes using an 8 mm drill bit, a spindle speed of 1000 rpm, and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, transforming the Gear Shaft into a drilled component placed back on the conveyor belt.

The broaching operation, performed on a broaching machine for 27 minutes using a pull broach with a feed rate of 0.2 mm/stroke and a depth of cut of 0.5 mm, transforms a metal bar gear shaft on a conveyor belt into a broached component gear shaft on the same conveyor belt.

The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on a BroachedComponent Gear Shaft for 61 minutes at a hobbing speed of 50 rpm, a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, and an involute gear profile, transforming it into a HobbiedGear Gear Shaft.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning on a Gear Shaft, using the CNC program 'GearShaft_Final' with a spindle speed of 1500 rpm and tool offsets of 0.01 mm, transforming the lathed part into a finished machined component on the conveyor belt in 10 minutes.

The Gear Shaper machine performs Gear Shaping on a BroachedComponent Gear Shaft from the ConveyorBelt for 67 minutes at a speed of 30 strokes/min to produce a ShapedGear with 20 Spur-type teeth, which is then placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Milling on a Gear Shaft placed on the ConveyorBelt, contouring it at a speed of 2000 rpm to achieve a surface finish of 0.4 Ra, producing a finished machined component on the ConveyorBelt in 21 minutes.

The Grinding operation uses a Grinding Machine with an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel rotating at 2000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass to transform a Gear Shaft from a PlanedPart to a GroundPart, processed on a ConveyorBelt for 90 minutes.

The threading operation is performed on a Screw Machine for 73 minutes, using a lathed Gear Shaft from a conveyor belt as input, to produce a screwed Gear Shaft with M10 metric threads at a rate of 10 parts per minute, which is then placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Vertical Milling Machine mills the lathed Gear Shaft into a milled Gear Shaft using an End Mill at 1500 rpm with a depth of cut of 2 mm for 14 minutes, with both input and output components remaining on the Conveyor Belt.

Using a Shaper machine for 17 minutes, the MilledPart1 from the ConveyorBelt is transformed into ShapedPart1 through the Shaping operation with a stroke length of 500mm, a shaping speed of 25mm/s, and a high-speed steel (HSS) tool, with the final product placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Gear Shaping operation uses a Gear Shaper to transform a BroachedComponent (BroachedComponent1) from the ConveyorBelt into a ShapedGear (ShapedGear1) on the same ConveyorBelt, shaped as a 24-tooth Spur gear at a speed of 30mm/s, for 37 minutes.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs horizontal milling for 21 minutes at a milling speed of 1500rpm, using a contour tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8, transforming the MilledPart2 component into the FinishedMachinedComponent1, with both components handled on the conveyor belt.

The shearing operation on the Shear (Sheet Metal) machine transforms SheetMetal1 from the conveyor belt into ShearedSheetMetal1, using a high carbon steel blade at a shear angle of 2 degrees and a cutting speed of 10m/min, for 91 minutes.

The Screw Machining operation processes LathedPart1 on Screw Machines for 7 minutes, using an M6 screw with a metric thread type at a production rate of 60pcs/min, transforming it into ScrewedComponent1 which is then placed on the conveyor belt.
Using a Punch Press for 44 minutes, the operation punches SheetMetal2 into FinishedSheetMetalProduct1 with a 10mm punch size, a stroke speed of 30spm, and a die alignment of 0.02mm.

Using a CNC Turning Center, the CNC Turning operation transforms LathedPart2 from the ConveyorBelt into FinishedMachinedComponent2 on the same ConveyorBelt, applying the CustomProgram1 CNC program with tool offsets X=0.00 Z=0.00 and a spindle speed of 1200rpm, for 22 minutes.

The Vertical Lathe performs Vertical Lathe Turning on MetalBar1, which is delivered by a MobileRobot, for 50 minutes at a rotation speed of 800rpm using a Carbide Insert tool with a feed rate of 0.2mm/rev to produce LathedPart3, which is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The Honing operation refines the surface of HonedCylinder1 using a Honing Machine with a 400 grit size, a 90s cycle time, and a target bore size of 50mm, transforming it into PrecisionFinishedPart1 in 31 minutes.
Using a bandsaw, MetalBar2 is cut into LathedPart4 for 82 minutes at a saw speed of 50m/min with a bi-metal blade and a cutting width of 2mm.
The Vertical Milling Machine performs vertical milling on LathedPart5 for 53 minutes at a milling speed of 1800rpm using an end mill with a depth of cut of 5mm, transforming it into MilledPart3.

The Planer machine performs a Planing operation for 21 minutes, transforming MilledPart4 from the conveyor belt into PlanedPart1 with a planing depth of 1.5mm, a feed rate of 0.3mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6.

The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on SheetMetal3 for 89 minutes using a laser power of 2000W, a cutting speed of 5m/min, and nitrogen gas assist, transforming the sheet metal into CutSheetMetal1.

The Grinding operation, performed on Grinding Machines for 35 minutes using an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at a wheel speed of 30m/s and a feed rate of 0.02mm/rev, transforms PlanedPart2 into GroundPart1, both transported on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) operating at 240V 10A with a brass wire and a cutting speed of 6mm/min, the ShapedPart2 from the conveyor belt is precision-cut into PrecisionFinishedPart2 over a duration of 48 minutes.

The Stewart Platform Milling operation transforms MilledPart5 into GroundPart2 using Stewart Platform Mills for 16 minutes with a milling precision of 0.01mm, a standard tool configuration, and active vibration damping.

The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on BroachedComponent2 for 70 minutes at a hobbing speed of 100rpm, a feed rate of 0.1mm/rev, and a helical gear profile, transforming it into HobbiedGear1, which is then placed on the conveyor belt.

The Drilling operation uses a Drill Press to drill a 6mm hole into MetalBar3, which is sourced from a ConveyorBelt, at a spindle speed of 1200rpm and a feed rate of 0.15mm/rev, transforming it into DrilledComponent1, placed back on the ConveyorBelt, and the process takes 93 minutes.

The Broaching Machine performs a broaching operation on MetalBar4 using a pull broach tool with a feed rate of 0.05mm per stroke and a depth of cut of 0.5mm for 41 minutes, transforming it into BroachedComponent3 on the ConveyorBelt.

Perform Horizontal Lathe Turning on a Horizontal Lathe for 5 minutes using a ceramic insert tool at 600rpm and a feed rate of 0.15mm/rev to transform MetalBar5 into LathedPart6, which is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Shaper machine performs Gear Shaping for 63 minutes, using a Carbide Cutter with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 25 m/min, to transform a MilledPart Gear Blank from the ConveyorBelt into a ShapedPart Shaped Gear Blank placed onto a MobileRobot.

The Planer performs Gear Planing on a Gear Blank taken from the ConveyorBelt for 68 minutes with a planing depth of 5 mm, a feed rate of 0.2 m/min, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2, resulting in a Planed Gear Blank placed on the MobileRobot.

The Gear Punching operation, performed on a Punch Press for 45 minutes, uses a 20 mm punch at a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min with a die alignment of 0.1 mm to transform a SheetMetal Gear Plate from the ConveyorBelt into a FinishedSheetMetalProduct Punched Gear Plate, which is then placed on a MobileRobot.

A Broaching Machine performs Gear Broaching on a MetalBar Gear Shaft from the ConveyorBelt using a Helical broach at a feed rate of 0.15 m/min and a depth of cut of 2 mm, transforming it into a Broached Gear Shaft placed on a MobileRobot, for 41 minutes.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs Gear Milling on a LathedPart Gear Blank from the ConveyorBelt to produce a Milled Gear Blank, placed on a MobileRobot, using a Milling speed of 3000 rpm, an End Mill tool, and a Depth of cut of 3 mm, for 78 minutes.

Perform Gear Hobbing on a Hobbing Machine for 74 minutes at a hobbing speed of 200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 m/min to transform a BroachedComponent Gear Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a HobbiedGear, which is then placed on a MobileRobot, using an Involute gear profile.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs Gear Grinding on a Gear Blank from the ConveyorBelt for 97 minutes using a CBN Wheel with a milling precision of 0.02 mm and active vibration damping, producing a Ground Gear Blank that is placed on a MobileRobot.

The Gear Grinding operation, performed on a Grinding Machine for 14 minutes, uses an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at 3000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 m/min to transform a planed Gear Blank from the Conveyor Belt into a ground Gear Blank, which is then placed on a Mobile Robot.

The Gear Shaping operation, performed on a Gear Shaper for 48 minutes at a shaping speed of 20 m/min, transforms a BroachedComponent Gear Blank from the ConveyorBelt into a Shaped Gear with 24 teeth of Spur type, which is then placed on a MobileRobot.

The Bandsaw performs the Gear Cutting operation for 54 minutes, using a bimetal blade at a speed of 50 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm, to transform the MetalBar Gear Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into the LathedPart Cut Gear Shaft placed on the MobileRobot.

The Gear Turning operation is performed on a CNC Turning Center for 91 minutes, using a Custom Gear Profile CNC program with tool offsets of 0.05 mm and a spindle speed of 2500 rpm, to transform the Gear Shaft from the conveyor belt into a Finished Gear Shaft placed on a mobile robot.

The Horizontal Lathe performs Gear Turning on a MetalBar Gear Shaft from the ConveyorBelt for 92 minutes, using a Carbide Insert tool at a rotation speed of 300 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 m/min, producing a Turned Gear Shaft that is placed on a MobileRobot.

The 'Gear Shearing' operation, performed on the Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 91 minutes, cuts the Gear Plate with a 1° shear angle and a cutting speed of 0.5 m/min using a High-Speed Steel blade, transforming it into the Sheared Gear Plate, which is then placed on a MobileRobot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Gear Milling on a Gear Blank, using a milling speed of 3500 rpm, a contour tool path, and achieving a surface finish of Ra 1.6, transforming the Gear Blank into a Finished Gear Blank in 64 minutes.

The Honing Machine performs Gear Honing on a Gear Bore using a 320-grit honing tool with a 5-minute cycle time and a 50 mm bore size for 61 minutes, transforming the HonedCylinder on the ConveyorBelt into a PrecisionFinishedPart placed on a MobileRobot.

The Gear Finishing operation uses a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) to precisely shape a Gear Blank into a Finished Gear Blank, operating at 20 A, 100 V with a brass wire and a cutting speed of 10 mm/min for 6 minutes, with the input component moving from the conveyor belt and the output being placed on a mobile robot.

The Gear Threading operation is performed on Screw Machines for 6 minutes, using an M6 metric screw size at a production rate of 50 pcs/min, to transform a lathed Gear Shaft from the conveyor belt into a Screwed Gear Shaft placed on a mobile robot.

The Gear Cutting operation uses a Laser Cutter to precisely cut a SheetMetal Gear Plate from the ConveyorBelt into a Cut Gear Plate, placed on a MobileRobot, using a laser power of 2000 W, a cutting speed of 1 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist, and takes 60 minutes to complete.

The Gear Drilling operation uses a Drill Press to drill an 8 mm hole in a Gear Plate (a MetalBar component taken from the ConveyorBelt) with a spindle speed of 1500 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 m/min, producing a Drilled Gear Plate (a DrilledComponent) placed on a MobileRobot, and the process takes 65 minutes.

The Gear Turning operation on a Vertical Lathe machines a Gear Shaft from a MetalBar into a Turned Gear Shaft using a Ceramic Insert tool at 400 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 m/min, taking 73 minutes to complete before the part is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The Gear Shaper machine performs the Gear Shaping operation on a BroachedComponent Gear Blank from the ConveyorBelt for 91 minutes, shaping a 24-tooth Spur gear at 120 RPM, resulting in a ShapedGear Finished Gear placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a Punch Press, the operation of Punching transforms Sheet Metal from the Conveyor Belt into a Punched Sheet placed on the Mobile Robot, taking 58 minutes with a punch size of 10 mm, a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min, and a die alignment of 0.1 mm.
Using Screw Machines, the Threading operation transforms a LathedPart Rod from the ConveyorBelt into an M8 Metric ScrewedComponent Screw at a production rate of 50 units/min, for 75 minutes.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Finishing Milling on a Block for 11 minutes at a milling speed of 2000 RPM using a linear tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8, transforming the Block into a Milled Block.

The Precision Turning operation, performed on a CNC Turning Center for 7 minutes using the Turnex 1.0 CNC program, tool offsets of X0.01 and Z0.005, and a spindle speed of 1500 RPM, transforms a Cylinder from the ConveyorBelt into a Turned Cylinder, which is then placed back on the ConveyorBelt as a FinishedMachinedComponent.

The Shaper machine performs the Shaping operation for 86 minutes, transforming a MilledPart Block from the ConveyorBelt into a ShapedPart Shaped Block using a HSS tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 20 strokes/min.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs Wire Cutting for 70 minutes on a ShapedPart Block from the ConveyorBelt, using a Brass wire at 100 V, 10 A, and a cutting speed of 5 mm/min, to produce a PrecisionFinishedPart EDM Finished Block placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs a Vertical Milling operation for 26 minutes on a lathed cylinder from the conveyor belt, using an end mill at 1800 RPM with a depth of cut of 2 mm, transforming it into a milled cylinder placed back on the conveyor belt.
